title: The Supreme Court's 'Shadow Docket'
hook: Most Supreme Court rulings today aren't fully-argued opinions — they're fast, often unsigned orders with little explanation. In the term ending October 2025, those quietly became the majority.
key_points: The 'shadow docket' is the Court's emergency track: it skips full briefing and oral argument, and often skips a full written opinion too.
In the term ending October 2025, the Court issued 63 shadow-docket orders versus 56 argued merits decisions — more emergency orders than full rulings, a first.
Only about 17% of shadow-docket votes come with any public record of how each justice voted or why.
The Trump administration filed 32 emergency applications in 2025 alone, versus 8 combined from the Bush and Obama administrations over the prior 16 years.
Justice Elena Kagan has called the trend 'unreasoned, inconsistent, and impossible to defend.'
content_html: The Supreme Court most people picture — full briefs, a public oral argument, a signed opinion months later — is only part of how the Court actually rules. The other part is the "shadow docket": an emergency track for urgent requests, built to move fast, with little of the paper trail that comes with a normal case.
extra_html: Per ProPublica's Ken B. Morales, the term ending October 2025 crossed a line: the Court issued 63 shadow-docket orders against just 56 argued merits decisions — the first time emergency orders have outnumbered full rulings. Transparency lags the volume: only around 17% of shadow-docket votes come with any public record of how individual justices voted or why. Use of the track has also surged on one side of the docket — the Trump administration filed 32 emergency applications in 2025 alone, compared with 8 combined from the Bush and Obama administrations across the previous 16 years. Legal scholars have flagged the pattern, and Justice Elena Kagan has described the trend in her own writing as "emblematic of too much of this Court's shadow docket decisionmaking — which every day becomes more unreasoned, inconsistent, and impossible to defend." The underlying civics point holds regardless of who occupies the White House: a court's emergency powers can, over time, become its ordinary way of doing business — with far less public reasoning attached. (This card describes U.S. Supreme Court practice specifically.)

related.title: How the Supreme Court Decides a Case
related.hook: A top court hears only a sliver of the cases that beg for its attention — and the path from petition to ruling runs through written briefs, a public argument, and a vote taken in secret.

related.title: The Judiciary & Judicial Review
related.hook: Courts don't just settle disputes between people — through judicial review, many can also strike down a law or an official act that violates the constitution.

related.title: Accountability & Oversight
related.hook: Power left unwatched drifts toward abuse. Accountability is the demand that officials answer for what they do — and oversight is the machinery that makes them.

related.title: Not All Dissents Are Created Equal
related.hook: Dissent tallies treat a one-line 'I would deny' the same as a fully reasoned opinion. One scholar sorted 386 of them on the emergency docket — and found about half were just bare votes.

flashcards.back_html: Its emergency track for urgent applications — it bypasses full briefing and oral argument, and often produces no full written opinion either.

flashcards.prompt: What milestone did the Court's term ending October 2025 mark?

choices.text: More shadow-docket orders (63) than argued merits decisions (56) — a first
The shadow docket was formally abolished
Every emergency order came with a full written opinion

flashcards.explanation_html: For the first time in modern history, the Court's emergency orders outnumbered its fully-argued rulings.

flashcards.prompt: What's the main criticism raised about how the shadow docket is used?

choices.text: Only a small share of votes come with any public reasoning or recorded vote
It requires a unanimous vote of all nine justices
It can only be used for tax cases
